extracted.intended_audience: external experts invited to provide written reviews for Wellcome funding applications (prospective Wellcome reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for experts asked to provide a written review of a shortlisted Wellcome grant application: what to assess, procedural steps, confidentiality, and how to avoid bias when answering scheme-specific questions (usually up to seven).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess significance and potential impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Help the advisory committee better understand the significance and potential impact of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should comment on how the project could advance knowledge or techniques and the importance of the problem being addressed; these comments help committees evaluate significance and potential impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess feasibility and appropriateness of the proposed approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Help the advisory committee better understand how feasible the project is and whether the proposed approach is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the study design, methods and proposed approach are suitable to deliver the anticipated outcomes and address the research questions; flag concerns about feasibility or methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate whether the research is 'bold'
rubrics_metrics.description: Is it likely to generate new insights or tools that will significantly advance existing knowledge or techniques?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state whether the work is likely to produce transformative or high‑risk/high‑reward advances; consider the degree to which the proposal pushes boundaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate whether the research is 'creative'
rubrics_metrics.description: Will it develop and test new concepts, methods or technologies, or combine existing ideas and approaches in new way?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess novelty in concepts, methods or combinations of approaches; consider whether the proposal tests new ideas or applies methods in novel combinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate overall research quality (design)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is it designed in a way that will address the research questions and deliver the anticipated outcomes?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge the scientific rigor and clarity of the research design, including appropriateness of methods, controls, analysis plans and whether the plan is likely to produce reliable results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment on use of animals where applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: If the proposed research involves animals, comment on whether this is justified and appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should assess ethical and scientific justification for animal use, appropriateness of species and numbers, and whether alternatives have been considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base the review only on the information provided (no extra background research)
rubrics_metrics.description: We are only asking for your feedback on the research proposal. Base your review on the information we have provided, and nothing else.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not search for or use external information about the applicant, their institution, or publications; this keeps all reviewers using the same evidence and improves consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declare when questions are outside your expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Tell Wellcome if you don’t feel confident answering any of the questions in the expert review form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a question is outside your expertise, notify Wellcome so they can assign another reviewer; you are not expected to know everything.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not judge applications on grammar or spelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on what the proposal says rather than how the applicant is saying it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid penalising applicants for imperfect English; consider reasons such as non-native language, lack of institutional support, or dyslexia. 'Flawed English' does not mean 'flawed research.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not delegate the review to someone else
rubrics_metrics.description: Don’t ask someone else to complete the review in your name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you cannot do the review, tell Wellcome. They selected you for your specific expertise and must check conflicts of interest for the person doing the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not penalise different methodological approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Don’t base your review on whether the applicant does things in the same way as you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on the merit of the proposal rather than whether it follows your own methods; penalising different approaches risks missing new solutions and disproportionately affects underrepresented groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware of and try to avoid bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Take time to think about the feedback you’re giving and whether it might be biased.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strive to make feedback objective and fair throughout the review process; reflect on possible unconscious biases that might affect your judgement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agree to confidentiality before viewing materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Agree to a confidentiality agreement before you can view a summary of the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must accept the confidentiality terms on the Wellcome platform prior to accessing application materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow scheme‑specific questions (answer up to 7 questions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Read the research proposal and answer up to 7 questions about the proposal, designed specifically for each funding scheme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The expert review is completed online; questions are tailored to the funding scheme and you should answer them directly and concisely as part of the review submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer selection is based on expertise (not career stage) and can be cross‑sector and international
rubrics_metrics.description: Wellcome chooses external expert reviewers based on their expertise in the research or the proposed techniques; reviewers can work in any sector and be from any country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers may be from academia, industry, policy organisations or think tanks; applicants may suggest reviewers but Wellcome does not have to use those suggestions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical/process notes: online completion, account, conflicts, word limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete the review online after creating a Wellcome Funding account, agreeing confidentiality, and declaring conflicts; research proposals will normally be no more than 3,000 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process steps: accept invitation, create account, agree confidentiality, view summary and declare conflicts, agree to review, read proposal (normally ≤3,000 words), answer questions, submit. You can optionally provide anonymised diversity information.
